name: Interface Router
description: Orchestration layer above individual panels: lazy-loads interface modules on first navigation, keeps a back stack, drives enter/exit transitions, and broadcasts theme changes to every loaded view. The library supplies many leaf panels (hud, inventory_panel, dialogue_box) but nothing that owns which one is showing, so that role currently falls to per-project glue. Navigation is an inbound API call rather than an event, since the router is the authority on its own stack and a request event with no declared emitter would be a dangling edge; the router reports outcomes as events instead. Each registered view implements an optional Show/Hide/SetContext/OnThemeChanged surface and the router calls only what a view actually declares. Exit animation and teardown run on a detached thread so navigation never blocks the caller.

implementations.note: Contract only. Intentionally left unimplemented pending a decision on view registration style - descriptor table versus module self-registration.

provenance: Surfaced by the same defect pass (2026-09-11), where a hand-rolled MasterUIController owned lazy loading, a back stack, transitions and theme broadcast for nine panels, which is the per-project glue this library exists to remove. Searched first: ui.hud renders a layer a brick publishes, ui.inventory_panel and ui.dialogue_box are leaves that open and close themselves, ui.passage_engine walks a story graph rather than a view stack; nothing owns which interface is currently showing. Library-native; left unimplemented pending a view-registration decision.
